thread.title: Starbucks: Digital Is the Key to Same-Store Sales Growth

author: David Marino-Nachison
title: Starbucks: Digital Is the Key to Same-Store Sales Growth
text:
Photo: Agence France-Presse/Getty Images By David Marino-Nachison June 7, 2018 11:37 a.m. ET If you follow Starbucks (SBUX), chances are you hear the word “flywheel” — an engineering term describing, roughly, a device that stores and distributes energy — a lot, with management using it to describe its use of digital technology to keep customers engaged.
That flywheel is why many see the Barron’s Next 50 company as a technological leader in food and drink — but it’s also seen as a necessity as the company seeks to sustain growth in the U.S. market and beyond . On Thursday, UBS said Starbucks and Domino’s (DPZ) “look best positioned on digital.”
More About Barron’s Next Learn more about Barron’s Next The Barron’s Next 50 “Starbucks’ digital flywheel has been the largest single contributor to U.S. comp growth in recent quarters,” UBS analysts wrote. “We expect digital/loyalty will be the most meaningful driver of same-store sales in coming quarters as well.” (You know what else might help? A recent price increase , as the Wall Street Journal noted today.)
The flywheel, generally, describes a set of digital services that address rewards, ordering, payment and personalized information and offers. The company recently told investors to expect same-store sales growth on the “low end” of the 3-5% range for the current fiscal year.
Starbucks’ size is part of the reason the flywheel works, according to UBS, which estimated that the company’s leading share of coffee app downloads — compared to Dunkin’ Brands Group ’s (DNKN), among others — has outperformed its broader market share this year.
Illustration: UBS “As Starbucks continues to enhance app features, including suggested sell, one-to-one marketing, and personalized offers, we expect continued outperformance and share leadership,” UBS wrote.
Newsletter Sign-up A recent eMarketer report said that Starbucks’s mobile payment service would be used by more Americans than those of tech heavyweights Apple (AAPL), Alphabet’s (GOOGL) Google, and others, in 2018.
Starbucks recently announced that Chairman Howard Schultz would step down ; he’d previously handed over the CEO’s job on two occasions.
